name: Proper Equivalence Queries Complexity / Star Number
details: For every finite binary concept class, $\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{peq}}(\mathcal H)\geq\mathrm S(\mathcal H)$.
proof: Proper equivalence-query complexity is projection-monotone: a projected learner simulates the original learner using a lift of the projected target, and any projected counterexample is a valid counterexample to the original query.  Applying $\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{peq}}\geq\mathrm{TD}$ to every coordinate projection gives $\mathrm{Q}_{\mathrm{peq}}(\mathcal H)\geq\max_{T\subseteq X}\mathrm{TD}(\mathcal H_{|T})=\mathrm{TS}_{\max}^p(\mathcal H)$.  The latter parameter equals the star number.
proof_source: Database-owned proper-equivalence-query/teaching argument, projection-monotonicity evidence for Proper Equivalence Queries Complexity, and the Star Number / Maximum Projected Teaching Set Size equality.
witness_verification: For half-intervals, proper equivalence-query complexity is $\log_2 n$, whereas the star number (equivalently maximum projected teaching-set size) is $2$.
